outcome: Incidence of umbilical cord around the neck
cohort: 1358 patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) from an unspecified location, including 484 in 2018, 468 in 2019, and 406 in 2020 (home quarantine group)
finding: Home quarantine during the COVID-19 outbreak was associated with higher glycemic levels and a greater likelihood of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including higher cesarean section rates, lower Apgar scores, and increased incidence of macrosomia and umbilical cord around the neck, in women with GDM.
mod_finding: The study found that patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) who experienced home quarantine during the COVID-19 outbreak had higher cesarean section rates compared to previous years.
birth_weight: Neonatal weight was a primary outcome measure, noting that home quarantine was associated with higher glycemic levels and potentially impacting neonatal weight.
